item.title: Setting Up at a Campsite
item.description: Learn words for putting up a tent, getting ready to sleep outdoors, and taking the tent down in the morning.

children.definition: A small shelter made of cloth that you can sleep in outdoors.
children.example: Our tent has enough room for two adults and their bags.

children.definition: A warm bag that you get inside to sleep outdoors.
children.example: I left my sleeping bag inside the tent so it would be ready at bedtime.

children.definition: A waterproof sheet covering the ground inside or beneath a tent.
children.example: We put the groundsheet on the grass before we put up the tent.
children.translation_uz: chodir ichiga yoki tagiga yoziladigan suv oʻtkazmaydigan toʻshama

children.definition: A short piece of metal or plastic that goes into the ground to hold part of a tent in place.
children.example: One peg is still in the ground at the front of the tent.
collocations: push a peg into the ground

children.definition: A long, thin rod that supports a tent.
children.example: The last tent pole goes across the top, just above the door.
collocations: fit a tent pole into place

children.definition: A small electric light that you can hold in your hand.
children.example: I used my torch to find my shoes outside the tent after dark.

children.definition: A place where people can put up tents and stay for the night.
children.example: The campsite has space for six tents near the lake.
children.translation_uz: chodir tikib tunash mumkin boʻlgan joy

children.definition: To put up a tent so people can use it.
children.example: We can pitch our tent beside yours before it gets dark.
collocations: pitch a tent on the grass

children.definition: A thin pad you put on the ground to lie on when you sleep outdoors.
children.example: I put my sleeping mat inside the tent and placed my bag by my feet.
children.translation_uz: yerga yozib, ustida uxlash uchun moʻljallangan yupqa toʻshama

children.definition: A piece of fabric that covers an opening in a tent.
children.example: I unzipped the tent flap and put our bags inside.

children.definition: A thin rope that goes from the side of a tent to the ground and helps hold the tent in place.
children.example: I found a spare guy rope in the tent bag.
collocations: tie a guy rope to a peg

children.definition: To open something by pulling its zip open.
children.example: Can you unzip the tent door so I can bring the mats inside?

children.definition: To remove a tent from its standing position so you can pack it away.
children.example: We’ll take down the tent after breakfast on Sunday.
collocations: take down the tent in the morning

children.definition: To make something like a sheet lie flat over an area.
children.example: Let’s spread out the groundsheet beside the car before we put up the tent.
